short: Kenya's Artificial Intelligence Bill, 2026 (Senate Bills No. 4 of 2026) awaits second reading in the Senate; the Data Protection Act, 2019 is the binding law, with fines of up to KES 5 million or 1% of turnover, whichever is lower.
title: Kenya AI Laws
subtitle: The Artificial Intelligence Bill, 2026 in the Senate, and the Data Protection Act
body_html:
Status at a glance

AI bill pending. The Artificial Intelligence Bill, 2026 (Senate Bills No. 4 of 2026), published in the Kenya Gazette Supplement on 19 February 2026 and read a first time on 2 April 2026, would create an Office of the Artificial Intelligence Commissioner and a risk-tiered regime. It awaits second reading; the Senate ICT committee's report on it was listed to be laid on 7 October 2026. The Data Protection Act, 2019 is the binding law today. The government is also consulting on a draft AI and Emerging Technologies Policy (July 2026) that proposes its own governance act. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Parliament of Kenya, the ICT ministry and the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateStatus
The Artificial Intelligence Bill, 2026Senate Bills No. 4 of 2026; Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 15Published 19 February 2026; first reading 2 April 2026Awaiting second reading
Data Protection Act, 2019No. 24 of 2019 (Cap. 411C); Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 18111 November 2019In force
Kenya AI Strategy 2025 to 2030Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital EconomyLaunch set for 27 March 2025; implementation roadmap December 2025Policy
Draft Kenya AI and Emerging Technologies PolicyDraftJuly 2026Consultation draft

Who regulates and enforces

  • Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC): enforces the Data Protection Act, including section 35 on automated decisions.
  • Office of the Artificial Intelligence Commissioner: proposed by the bill (cl. 4 onward).
  • Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy: AI strategy and policy.

Scope and reach

The bill would cover providers, deployers and users of AI systems (cl. 2) and public entities, including county governments (cl. 34); it has no explicit extraterritorial clause. The Data Protection Act already reaches controllers and processors not established in Kenya that process personal data of data subjects located in Kenya (s. 4(b)(ii)).

Core obligations

  • Under the bill, if enacted: four risk tiers, unacceptable, high, limited and minimal (cl. 25); risk and human-rights impact assessments before deploying a high-risk system, records kept at least five years, and consent and AI labelling for use of a person's likeness or voice (cl. 26); a public register of high-risk systems (cl. 27); disclosure to users, human intervention in significant automated decisions and annual compliance reports (cl. 28); a workforce impact assessment (cl. 33).
  • Today: the Data Protection Act, including rights over solely automated decisions (s. 35).

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Data Protection Act infringementsUp to KES 5,000,000 or, for an undertaking, up to 1% of annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is lowerDPA s. 63ODPC
Under the bill, if enacted: deploying an unacceptable-risk system, an unassessed high-risk deployment, harmful non-consensual synthetic media and similar offencesA fine of up to KES 5,000,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or bothBill cl. 35(1) and 35(2)(a)Courts
Under the bill, if enacted: transparency failures, breach of ethical guidelines, obstructionA fine of up to KES 1,000,000, imprisonment of up to six months, or bothBill cl. 35(2)(b)Courts

What is coming next

  • The Senate ICT committee's report and the bill's second reading; the report was listed for 7 October 2026.
  • The final AI and Emerging Technologies Policy, which proposes drafting a governance act within six months and enacting it within twelve.

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: a press report that the committee recommended rejecting the bill, and the Data Protection Act's assent and commencement dates.
